hero.headline: Justice Department ends Trump administration anti-weaponization fund
hero.body:
The Justice Department told a federal court that the Trump administration's compensation fund for people who claimed they were targets of government weaponization will not continue. Two DOJ attorneys filed the notice in the Eastern District of Virginia, formally ending the nearly $1.8 billion program.

The fund was created by the Trump administration to compensate individuals who believed they were wrongly investigated or prosecuted for political reasons. The Justice Department's filing asked the court to reject a legal challenge brought by a former federal prosecutor and several other individuals related to the program.

The compensation fund represented one of the Trump administration's initiatives to address what it characterized as political targeting by federal law enforcement. The program's total budget allocation reached $1.8 billion before the Justice Department moved to discontinue it.

The court filing provides official confirmation that the program has been terminated. The former federal prosecutor and other plaintiffs had brought their challenge in Virginia's Eastern District, one of the busiest federal court districts in the country. The Justice Department's request for dismissal of that challenge coincided with its announcement that the fund would cease operations.

The end of the anti-weaponization fund marks a significant policy reversal. No information was provided about whether any compensation had been distributed before the program's termination or what will happen to the funds that had been set aside for the initiative.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange fire in Gulf as tensions escalate
cards.body:
The United States and Iran engaged in a series of military strikes on Saturday, marking the latest escalation in a conflict that has tested a fragile ceasefire established in April. The exchange underscores deepening tensions between the two powers and threatens ongoing diplomatic efforts to extend the truce.

The confrontation began when the US military shot down four Iranian attack drones headed toward the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping corridor through which roughly a fifth of global oil supplies transit. In response, American forces struck coastal surveillance radar sites on Sirik and Qeshm Island that officials said were involved in the attacks. US Central Command stated the Iranian drones "posed an immediate threat to regional maritime traffic" and the radar strikes were necessary to "defend against further attacks."

Hours later, Iran's Revolutionary Guards retaliated by launching missiles and drones at what they described as "enemy bases" in the Gulf region. The strikes targeted US military facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain, both of which activated air raid alerts. According to Central Command, Iran fired seven ballistic missiles toward Kuwait and Bahrain, with six successfully intercepted and a seventh failing to reach its target. The military reported no harm to US personnel and denied Iranian claims of damaging the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain.

Kuwait's military also reported responding to "hostile" missile and drone attacks. The strikes came days after a previous attack on Kuwait's international airport that killed one person and wounded dozens.

The latest escalation reflects broader complications undermining ceasefire negotiations. Both the United States and Iran have been working for weeks to extend the ceasefire by 60 days and initiate new discussions on Iran's nuclear program. However, both sides continue demanding changes to any potential agreement, with neither showing willingness to compromise.

President Donald Trump told reporters on Friday that the situation "seems to be going quite well," though he acknowledged the negotiations faced challenges. "It's a very hard thing" for Iran, Trump said, noting that Tehran faces demands it never expected to accept.

The fighting also extends to Lebanon, where Israeli forces have intensified bombing campaigns despite a ceasefire announced this week through US-brokered talks. However, Iranian-backed Hezbollah rejected the agreement, and both sides have launched new attacks. Iran has demanded that any lasting truce include provisions addressing the conflict in Lebanon, further complicating peace efforts.

The escalations highlight the precarious state of the region. The Strait of Hormuz remains a flashpoint in US-Iran relations, with Tehran previously threatening to restrict shipping during periods of heightened tension. As both sides continue military operations while pursuing negotiations, the balance between conflict and peace remains increasingly unstable.

cards.headline: Ukraine strikes St. Petersburg as Putin rejects peace talks
cards.teaser: Ukrainian drones targeted Russian military facilities in St. Petersburg for a second time as a major economic forum opened in the city.
cards.body:
Ukraine launched mass drone strikes against military facilities in St. Petersburg on Saturday, targeting an oil refinery and other military infrastructure in Russia's second-largest city. The attacks occurred on the final day of a major Russian economic forum.

The strikes followed Russian President Vladimir Putin's rejection of a peace offer from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. At the St. Petersburg forum, Putin dismissed Zelenskyy's open letter proposing face-to-face negotiations as rude and said he saw no point in meeting. Putin reaffirmed Russia's intention to achieve its war objectives, including seizing all of the Donbas region in eastern Ukraine.

cards.headline: Ebola spreads in East Africa as international response takes shape
cards.teaser: An Ebola outbreak in East Africa is prompting questions about which countries will lead the response effort.
cards.body:
The Ebola outbreak in central Africa is following a dangerous trajectory, according to modeling from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Computer projections show potential cases could range from 10,000 to more than 20,000—potentially matching the scale of the devastating 2014-2016 west African outbreak that killed more than 11,000 people.

The response is being hampered by ongoing conflict. Rebel attacks in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo have killed more than 30 people in recent days and disrupted Ebola containment efforts. At least three patients with Ebola fled clinics during the violence, complicating disease tracking and control measures.

cards.headline: Israel deploys white phosphorus munitions over populated areas in Lebanon
cards.teaser: Video evidence shows the Israeli military using white phosphorus munitions over populated regions of Lebanon.
cards.body:
The Israeli military has deployed white phosphorus munitions over populated areas in Lebanon, according to video evidence collected and analyzed by The Times. The munitions can cause severe harm to civilians and infrastructure when used in residential zones.

The deployment comes as the ceasefire in Lebanon shows signs of deteriorating. Israel has continued bombing campaigns in Lebanese territory despite the nominal ceasefire agreement, raising concerns about civilian casualties and the long-term viability of the truce.

cards.headline: Nasdaq Falls 4.2 Percent as Chip Stocks Tumble
cards.teaser: The Nasdaq composite dropped 4.2 percent on Friday, marking its steepest single-day decline since April 2025.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq composite dropped 4.2 percent on Friday, recording its worst day of the year. Semiconductor and technology stocks led the decline, with the S&P 500 also posting its worst day of 2026. The selloff reflected rising expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases, which weigh on growth-oriented tech companies with high valuations.

The sharp reversal wiped out gains accumulated over several weeks as investors reassessed holdings in AI-related equities. Traders cited persistent inflation readings as a factor fueling rate-hike odds. The speed of the decline suggested broad repositioning rather than company-specific developments, catching many investors off guard after months of steady gains driven by artificial intelligence enthusiasm.

cards.headline: Trump Considers Government Ownership Stake in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The Trump administration is discussing taking equity positions in leading artificial intelligence firms including OpenAI.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration is exploring the possibility of the federal government acquiring ownership stakes in top artificial intelligence companies. The discussions include OpenAI and could involve other leading AI firms. Meetings between Trump and AI company executives are expected as soon as next week to discuss potential government investment in exchange for equity.

The proposal would represent a significant shift in the government's relationship with private technology companies. Details about how such arrangements would be structured remain unclear. The administration has framed the discussions around ensuring American leadership in artificial intelligence development, though the legal and financial mechanisms for government equity participation have not been outlined.

cards.headline: Armenia holds election as Russia pressures pro-Western government
cards.teaser: Armenian voters head to the polls with incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeking a third term amid Russian pressure and falling domestic support.
cards.body:
Armenia is holding a parliamentary election as Russia intensifies pressure on the country's pro-Western government. Incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan is seeking a third term despite declining support at home.

The election represents a test of Armenia's orientation between Russia and the West. Pashinyan has moved to strengthen ties with Western nations, drawing pushback from Moscow, which has historically viewed Armenia as within its sphere of influence. The vote comes at a time when Russia is focused on maintaining allied governments in former Soviet states.

cards.headline: Pope Leo begins week-long visit to Spain
cards.teaser: Pope Leo arrived in Spain on Saturday for a visit that will include meetings with migrants and potential confrontations with far-right political forces.
cards.body:
Pope Leo arrived in Spain on Saturday for a weeklong visit. During his time there, he plans to meet with migrants and address social issues facing the country.

The trip comes as Spain grapples with increased secularization and political polarization. The Catholic Church's role in Spanish society remains complicated. The pontiff may face criticism from Vox, Spain's far-right party, which has opposed church positions on immigration and social policies.

cards.headline: European Union and China hold trade talks amid heightened tensions
cards.teaser: Trade officials from the European Union and China met to discuss escalating economic disputes between the two powers.
cards.body:
EU and Chinese trade officials met to discuss escalating tensions in their economic relationship. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has cautioned European nations about their economic dependence on China, a warning that has not convinced all EU members to change course.

The EU is developing new regulations to reduce reliance on Chinese manufacturing and materials by strengthening supply chain diversity. European trade officials say the bloc needs specific tools to address its dependencies on China, as Europe works to reconcile its economic interests with concerns about security and national sovereignty.

hero.headline: Forest Service plans office closures despite budget contradictions
hero.body:
The U.S. Forest Service has announced plans to close research facilities as part of a cost-cutting effort, but an analysis of the agency's financial data reveals internal inconsistencies. The agency stated it needs to reduce expenses to operate within its budget constraints, yet the proposed closures appear to target lower-cost operations while maintaining facilities with significantly higher operating costs.

According to the agency's figures, some of the research hubs slated for closure cost less than one dollar annually to rent. Meanwhile, the Forest Service plans to keep open at least one facility that carries an annual rental cost of one million dollars. The disparity has raised questions about the rationale behind the closure decisions and whether the moves will achieve the stated financial goals.

The Forest Service oversees research operations across the country that support forest management, wildlife conservation, and environmental monitoring. Research hubs typically house scientists and support staff who conduct studies on forest health, fire ecology, invasive species, and climate impacts. Closures would affect ongoing research projects and could result in staff relocations or job losses.

The agency has not provided detailed explanations for how it selected which facilities to close or how the closures align with its broader budget strategy. Critics have pointed to the cost analysis as evidence that the decision-making process may be driven by factors other than pure financial efficiency. Some observers suggest that real estate considerations, regional politics, or administrative preferences could be influencing which locations remain open.

The proposed closures come as federal agencies face pressure to reduce spending and demonstrate fiscal responsibility. The Forest Service, part of the Department of Agriculture, manages 193 million acres of national forests and grasslands. Research facilities play a role in informing management decisions across these lands, and their closure could have long-term implications for how the agency addresses challenges such as wildfire risk and ecosystem health.

cards.headline: Anthony Head, actor in Buffy and Ted Lasso, dies at 72
cards.teaser: The British actor died from complications related to pneumonia.
cards.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for his roles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso, has died at age 72. He died from complications related to pneumonia.

Head's career spanned several decades across television. Before his acclaimed roles in Buffy and Ted Lasso, he gained early public attention through 1980s Nescafe advertisements. He also appeared in the series Merlin and Little Britain.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra advances to California governor general election
cards.teaser: The Democrat will compete in the November election after advancing through the primary.
cards.body:
Democrat Xavier Becerra has advanced to California's November gubernatorial election after securing the top spot in the primary. His come-from-behind victory marks a significant moment in one of the state's most turbulent recent campaign seasons.

Election officials continue counting mail ballots to determine Becerra's general election opponent. The second-place finisher could be fellow Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist advocating for universal healthcare and higher taxes on billionaires, or Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality backed by Donald Trump.

cards.headline: Sikh community in Ohio documented preserving traditions
cards.teaser: A photographer has spent several years capturing the religious community's practices.
cards.body:
Photographer Akash Pamarthy has spent several years documenting the Sikh religious community in Ohio. Through his lens, he captures the ways this community actively works to maintain their religious practices and cultural heritage.

Pamarthy's photographic project illustrates how Ohio's Sikh population transmits their traditions and teachings to younger generations, ensuring that their faith and customs endure within the United States.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-0 lead over Spurs in NBA Finals
cards.teaser: New York won by one point and will return home two victories away from a championship.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs by one point in Game 2 to take a commanding 2-0 lead in the NBA Finals. Karl-Anthony Towns led the effort on both ends of the floor as New York held off a late Spurs rally. The Knicks became just the third team to win the first two Finals games on the road.

The series now returns to New York, where the Knicks are two wins away from clinching their first championship in generations. The historic Finals run marks a significant moment for the franchise and its fans, who have waited decades to see a title return to the capital.

cards.headline: Singer Duffy to perform first concert in over 15 years
cards.teaser: The Welsh singer stepped away from public life after a sexual assault.
cards.body:
Welsh singer Duffy has announced her first live concert in over 15 years, marking her return to performing after stepping away from public life. A sexual assault led to her extended absence from the music industry.

Duffy rose to prominence in the late 2000s before withdrawing from public appearances. This concert announcement signals her comeback to the stage.

cards.headline: Six charged after protest over Nowak death
cards.teaser: The men were remanded in custody and are scheduled to appear in court.
cards.body:
Six men have been charged with violent disorder following protests related to Henry Nowak's death. All six have been remanded in custody and are due to appear at Southampton Magistrates' Court.

The charges relate to their conduct during the demonstrations that took place after Nowak's death.

hero.headline: SpaceX Signs $30 Billion Computing Deal With Google
hero.teaser: SpaceX will lease computing capacity to Google for $920 million per month under a major cloud infrastructure agreement.
hero.body:
SpaceX has reached a $30 billion agreement to provide computing capacity to Google, marking one of the largest cloud computing contracts announced this year. Under the terms of the deal, Google will pay SpaceX approximately $920 million each month for access to computing power hosted at data centers operated by xAI, the artificial intelligence company founded by Elon Musk.

A Google representative attributed the agreement to unexpected demand for the company's recently launched AI products. The arrangement reflects the growing need for computing infrastructure to support artificial intelligence development across the technology industry.

The deal comes as SpaceX prepares for a potential initial public offering. The substantial recurring revenue from Google's monthly payments provides SpaceX with predictable income tied to the expanding demand for AI computing resources. This positions SpaceX to demonstrate consistent revenue streams to potential IPO investors.

The Google-SpaceX agreement follows similar patterns emerging across the industry. Other major technology firms have begun securing computing capacity through long-term contracts to support their AI development efforts. These arrangements signal a shift in how companies are approaching their infrastructure needs as artificial intelligence applications become more computationally demanding.

The partnership also comes amid broader developments regarding AI companies and government relationships. Google recently signed a separate agreement with the US Pentagon to make its artificial intelligence models available for classified government work. That contract allows the Pentagon to use Google's AI for "any lawful government purpose," according to reports. The Pentagon has signed agreements worth up to $200 million each with major AI labs including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.

However, Google's Pentagon agreement has generated significant internal controversy. More than 600 Google employees signed an open letter to CEO Sundar Pichai expressing concerns about the classified work arrangement. The employees stated they felt responsible for preventing unethical and dangerous uses of their technology, and urged the company to refuse making AI systems available for classified workloads.

The employees' concerns reflect longstanding tensions within Google over the company's involvement with military and surveillance applications. Last year, Alphabet, Google's parent company, lifted a ban on using AI for weapons and surveillance tools, removing language from its ethical guidelines that previously promised the company would not pursue "technologies that cause or are likely to cause overall harm."

Google's AI lead, Demis Hassabis, defended the shift by arguing that AI has become essential for protecting national security. The company has emphasized that it remains committed to consensus positions against domestic mass surveillance and autonomous weapons without human oversight.

The SpaceX computing deal represents Google's effort to meet surging demand for AI infrastructure, while the Pentagon agreement signals the technology company's deepening involvement in national security applications.

cards.headline: Nasdaq Falls 4.2 Percent as Chip Stocks Tumble
cards.teaser: The Nasdaq composite dropped 4.2 percent on Friday, marking its steepest single-day decline since April 2025.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq composite dropped 4.2 percent on Friday, recording its worst day of the year. Semiconductor and technology stocks led the decline, with the S&P 500 also posting its worst day of 2026. The selloff reflected rising expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate increases, which weigh on growth-oriented tech companies with high valuations.

The sharp reversal wiped out gains accumulated over several weeks as investors reassessed holdings in AI-related equities. Traders cited persistent inflation readings as a factor fueling rate-hike odds. The speed of the decline suggested broad repositioning rather than company-specific developments, catching many investors off guard after months of steady gains driven by artificial intelligence enthusiasm.

cards.headline: Anthropic Calls for Global Pause on AI Development
cards.teaser: The AI company warned that advanced systems capable of self-improvement pose risks of humans losing control.
cards.body:
Anthropic urged AI laboratories worldwide to consider pausing development of advanced artificial intelligence systems. The company flagged risks associated with AI that can improve itself, warning that humans could lose control over such systems. Anthropic argued that the industry should have the option to halt progress if safety concerns intensify.

The statement from Anthropic, itself a major AI developer, marks a notable departure from the rapid development pace maintained by most companies in the field. The call for a pause reflects growing debate within the AI community about whether current safety measures are adequate. Other major AI labs have not indicated they will slow their development timelines.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Tops List of Highest Paid CEOs
cards.teaser: Executive compensation is accelerating while rank-and-file workers see slower wage growth, widening the corporate pay gap.
cards.body:
Elon Musk led a list of the highest paid chief executives in corporate America. The data showed executive compensation continuing to accelerate, outpacing wage gains for typical workers. The gap between CEO pay and average employee compensation has widened in recent years.

The compensation figures include salary, bonuses, stock awards, and other forms of payment. Musk's pay package, tied heavily to Tesla stock performance, dwarfed that of other executives. The divergence between executive and worker pay has drawn scrutiny from labor advocates and some lawmakers, though corporate boards continue to approve large compensation packages they say are necessary to attract and retain top leadership.

cards.headline: S&P 500 Delays SpaceX Entry Despite Planned IPO
cards.teaser: New index rules may force SpaceX and other mega IPOs to wait years before joining the S&P 500.
cards.body:
SpaceX faces potential delays in joining the S&P 500 index even after completing its anticipated initial public offering. Index provider S&P Dow Jones Indices has established criteria that could block immediate entry for SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic. The rules demonstrate the power of index gatekeepers over which companies are included in benchmark indexes.

S&P 500 inclusion matters because trillions of dollars in passive investment funds automatically purchase stocks in the index. Exclusion means SpaceX would miss out on that automatic buying pressure, even as one of the largest newly public companies. The index provider created new fast-track provisions for older companies going public, but SpaceX may not qualify immediately. Some analysts noted SpaceX operates at a loss, which could further complicate its index eligibility.

cards.headline: WWE Shareholder Lawsuit Trial Removed From Court Schedule
cards.teaser: A Delaware trial over the TKO merger valuation has been taken off the calendar, delaying proceedings.
cards.body:
A trial in a WWE shareholder lawsuit challenging the company's merger with TKO has been removed from the Delaware Chancery Court's schedule. The case involves allegations that WWE was undervalued in the transaction. Plaintiffs filed pre-trial briefing arguing their position, but the trial date has been pulled.

Shareholders are seeking up to $957 million in damages related to the merger. The lawsuit contends that WWE stockholders did not receive fair value when the company combined with TKO. The removal from the court calendar spares WWE executives, including Vince McMahon, from immediate testimony. No new trial date has been set.

hero.headline: Microsoft AI chief says split from OpenAI frees company to pursue superintelligence
hero.body:
Microsoft's AI leadership stated the company has been liberated from its partnership with OpenAI and can now independently pursue advanced artificial intelligence development. The remarks emerged during Microsoft Build 2026, where the company introduced fresh AI models aimed at reducing dependency on OpenAI technology and cutting expenses for developers.

The declaration represents a major realignment in Microsoft and OpenAI's relationship, which had been defined by substantial Microsoft investments in the startup. Microsoft has constructed its own AI models to compete with OpenAI's offerings, expanding developer choices and potentially reducing licensing costs. At the conference, Microsoft positioned Windows as a trustworthy foundation for AI application development.

The divergence follows months of deteriorating relations between the two organizations. Microsoft served as OpenAI's primary cloud infrastructure supplier and major financial backer, but the partnership has frayed as each company pursues distinct strategies for advancing artificial intelligence. The Microsoft AI chief's assertion that the company had been "set free" hints that the collaboration had grown limiting rather than mutually beneficial.

During Build 2026, Microsoft focused on democratizing AI development and making it more economical for developers working with Windows. The company displayed infrastructure and tools supporting AI application creation independent of OpenAI's technology. Microsoft underscored security and trustworthiness capabilities positioned to make Windows the leading platform for constructing AI applications.

The separation enables Microsoft to engage in more direct competition with OpenAI in pursuing superintelligent systems. By advancing its own research agenda, Microsoft can establish independent technical priorities and development schedules without requiring coordination with OpenAI. This independence also allows Microsoft to retain greater value from AI systems built using its own infrastructure and resources.

The timing reflects broader industry dynamics. Anthropic, creator of the Claude chatbot, has surged ahead with a confidential IPO filing and recently surpassed OpenAI in valuation at 965 billion dollars following a 65 billion dollar funding round. Anthropic's Claude Code product has gained considerable traction with business clients, while its cybersecurity AI tool generated international attention for identifying bugs in widely used software. OpenAI's comparable products have struggled to achieve comparable market reception.

OpenAI is expected to file for its own public offering imminently, but the company appears to be losing ground in investor confidence and market perception. The reversal represents a significant loss of competitive advantage for ChatGPT's creator as the AI industry matures and valuations increasingly depend on demonstrated business performance rather than early-market positioning.

Meanwhile, Reid Hoffman has departed Microsoft's board after a profitable decade to focus on Manus, his AI drug discovery startup, signaling how prominent technology figures are reallocating attention across the rapidly evolving AI landscape.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy to conclude with Revelation in 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix revealed the third and final game in the Final Fantasy VII remake series will launch in spring 2027.
cards.body:
Square Enix announced Final Fantasy VII Revelation as the final installment of its remake trilogy, launching in spring 2027. The game will be available simultaneously across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. The company revealed the first trailer during Summer Game Fest Live, showcasing new footage and story elements.

The trilogy began with the original Final Fantasy VII Remake in 2020, followed by a sequel in 2024. Revelation will bring the reimagining of the classic 1997 game to a close.

cards.headline: LinkedIn founder Reid Hoffman leaves Microsoft board to focus on AI drug discovery startup
cards.teaser: Reid Hoffman stepped down from Microsoft's board of directors after a decade to concentrate on Manus, his artificial intelligence drug discovery company.
cards.body:
Reid Hoffman is stepping down from Microsoft's board after a decade of service to concentrate on Manus, his AI drug discovery startup. The move marks a shift toward a more hands-on leadership role at the biotech company.

Hoffman co-founded LinkedIn, which Microsoft acquired in 2016 for more than $26 billion. His departure from the board comes as he transitions to what's being called "founder mode" at Manus.

cards.headline: Guild Wars 3 announced for PC and PlayStation 5 with beta planned for 2027
cards.teaser: The third installment in the Guild Wars online role-playing game series was revealed at Summer Game Fest, set one thousand years before the original game.
cards.body:
ArenaNet announced Guild Wars 3 for personal computers and PlayStation 5, with a beta test scheduled for next year. The game represents what the developer calls a modern evolution of the massively multiplayer online role-playing game format, marking a significant update to the franchise.

Guild Wars 3 takes place one thousand years before the events of the first Guild Wars game, exploring an earlier period in the game world's timeline. The announcement addressed questions about the future of Guild Wars 2, which launched in 2012 and continues to operate with regular updates.

cards.headline: Stellar Blade sequel Blood Rain revealed with debut trailer
cards.teaser: Developer Shift Up announced a sequel to Stellar Blade featuring protagonist Evie, currently in development for PlayStation 5.
cards.body:
Shift Up unveiled Stellar Blade: Blood Rain, the sequel to its 2026 action game Stellar Blade, during Summer Game Fest 2026. The announcement included a debut trailer showcasing the continuation of the franchise.

Evie returns as the protagonist in Blood Rain, which is currently in development at the South Korean studio. The sequel will feature new gameplay and story elements building on the original PlayStation 5 exclusive.

cards.headline: The Wolf Among Us 2 set for 2027 release, remaster of original coming this year
cards.teaser: Telltale Games announced The Wolf Among Us 2 will launch in 2027, a decade after the sequel was first revealed, with a remaster of the original game arriving during the 2026 holiday season.
cards.body:
The Wolf Among Us 2 received a 2027 launch window at Summer Game Fest 2026, marking ten years since Telltale Games first announced the sequel. The studio also revealed a remaster of the original Wolf Among Us game, scheduled for release during the holiday season this year.

The Wolf Among Us Remastered will launch on Nintendo Switch, the upcoming Nintendo Switch 2, and other platforms. The game is based on the Fables comic book series and follows a detective investigating crimes in a community of fairy tale characters living in New York City.

cards.headline: Hitman Classic Trilogy remastered versions coming to Xbox in 2027
cards.teaser: IO Interactive announced remasters of the first three Hitman games for Xbox, PlayStation 5, and other platforms, scheduled for release in 2027.
cards.body:
The Hitman Classic Trilogy Remastered will bring updated versions of the original three Hitman games to modern consoles next year. IO Interactive revealed the collection at its IOI Access event, showcasing improved graphics and technical updates for the stealth assassination games originally released between 2000 and 2006.

The announcement included details about downloadable content featuring rapper Wiz Khalifa for the current Hitman games. IO Interactive is remastering the games that established the franchise before its more recent trilogy that concluded in 2021.

hero.headline: Scheffler and McIlroy trail by eight shots at Memorial Tournament
hero.teaser: The world's top two golfers struggled in their second rounds at the PGA Tour event.
hero.body:
The world's top two players both had difficult second rounds at the Memorial Tournament, leaving them well back in the field as the competition heads into Sunday's final round.

The leaderboard became unusually crowded after Saturday's play, with 21 players sitting within four shots of the lead. Alex Smalley, ranked 78th in the world, emerged atop the standings at six under par, holding a two-shot advantage over a five-way tie for second place.

Scottie Scheffler acknowledged the tightly bunched nature of the competition. "I've never seen anything like this," he said. "I've never seen a leaderboard this bunched up. It's quite literally anybody's tournament." Scheffler found himself five shots back after struggling with his putting on Saturday.

Rory McIlroy bounced back impressively from a difficult opening round. After shooting a poor first round where he made four consecutive bogeys and sat tied for 105th place, he carded a 66 on Saturday to move back into contention. "I've climbed my way out of that hole and I'm proud of myself for doing that," McIlroy said. "There's one more day left, and I feel like I'm close enough to the lead that I've still got a good chance."

McIlroy had been vocal about the difficulty of the course setup through the first two days. On Friday, both he and Scheffler complained about the pin placements. "When you have a set of greens like this, you can start to frustrate people pretty easily," McIlroy explained. He noted that while the challenging setup frustrated players, it created compelling entertainment for spectators. "If I wasn't playing this tournament, I'd love what's going on this week, but watching and playing are two different things," he said. "No profanity today," he added as he arrived to speak with the media.

The tournament committee appeared to adjust the difficulty on Saturday, moving pins to more accessible locations and benefiting from favorable weather conditions. The wind shifted and sunshine emerged, making some of the shorter par-fours reachable off the tee.

Smalley, making his first 54-hole lead in a professional tournament, had recovered from a rough start. He made four bogeys in his first eight holes before shooting five under par on his final ten holes. "I don't like being in the spotlight a whole lot," Smalley said. "I'm still trying to get used to playing in front of large groups of people like there are at tournaments like this one."

Jon Rahm, Xander Schauffele and Patrick Reed all sat just one shot behind Smalley. With such a congested leaderboard, Schauffele summed up Sunday's outlook: "It is going to be an absolute free-for-all."

cards.headline: Wembanyama reflects on costly late turnover in Spurs' Game 2 loss
cards.teaser: The Spurs center said urgency led to his critical mistake in the closing minutes of the NBA Finals game.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama's crucial turnover with 9.5 seconds remaining sealed the Spurs' 105-104 loss to the Knicks in Game 2 of the NBA Finals. The turnover allowed Jalen Brunson to sink the go-ahead free throw, and Wembanyama's subsequent shot from the elbow bounced off the back rim at the buzzer.

The second-year center acknowledged that urgency caused the error and said he would channel his frustration into preparation for Game 3. With the Spurs trailing 2-0, the series now shifts to Madison Square Garden, where the Knicks sit two wins away from their first championship in over 50 years.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-0 lead in NBA Finals with road win over Spurs
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in Game 2 of the NBA Finals on Friday night, taking a 2-0 series lead.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in Game 2 of the NBA Finals on Friday night, securing a 2-0 series lead. Karl-Anthony Towns delivered a complete performance on both ends of the floor, helping the Knicks hold off a late Spurs rally in the road victory. New York became just the third team in NBA history to win the first two Finals games away from home.

The series now shifts to Madison Square Garden for Game 3. Victor Wembanyama committed a costly turnover late in the game that proved decisive in the outcome. The Knicks are one step closer to their first NBA championship in generations, while the Spurs face an uphill climb to avoid falling into a 3-0 deficit.

cards.headline: 15-year-old Sooryavanshi earns first India call-up
cards.teaser: The teenage batting prospect made the T20 squad for tours of England and Ireland.
cards.body:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, has received his first international call-up after being named in India's T20 squad for upcoming matches against England and Ireland. The teenage sensation earned selection following an impressive IPL campaign where he amassed 776 runs at a strike rate of 237.30 and secured the tournament's most valuable player award.

Sooryavanshi is set to become India's youngest debutant since Sachin Tendulkar, marking a significant milestone in his cricket career. His selection demonstrates the selectors' confidence in the opening batsman's exceptional talent and potential at the international level.

cards.headline: NCAA denies Texas Tech appeal for quarterback Sorsby
cards.teaser: The governing body rejected the school's request to reinstate the transfer's eligibility.
cards.body:
The NCAA has rejected Texas Tech's appeal to reinstate quarterback Brendan Sorsby's eligibility, according to multiple reports. The ruling means Sorsby will be unavailable for the Red Raiders this season.

The decision upholds the NCAA's original determination regarding Sorsby's transfer status, ending the quarterback's prospects of playing for Texas Tech during the current campaign.

cards.headline: Judge says rib injury originated from April dive
cards.teaser: The Yankees outfielder traced his stress fracture to a play in late April.
cards.body:
Aaron Judge has identified the source of his right rib stress fracture. The Yankees outfielder traced the injury back to a diving play he made while attempting to field a ball in late April.

Judge's explanation connects his current ailment to that specific incident from earlier in the season, providing clarity on how the stress fracture developed.

cards.headline: NBA interviews Leonard in Clippers salary cap probe
cards.teaser: League investigators spoke with the star and his business adviser about alleged cap circumvention.
cards.body:
Kawhi Leonard and his business adviser have been interviewed by NBA investigators as part of a league probe into the Los Angeles Clippers. The investigation centers on allegations that the team circumvented salary cap rules to compensate the star forward.

The interviews represent the latest step in the NBA's examination of whether the Clippers violated league compensation regulations.

hero.headline: Actor Anthony Head dies at 72 from pneumonia complications
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications due to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," his daughters said.

Head's most iconic role was as the mentor and librarian Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, which ran from 1997 to 2003. In the show, he served as a father figure to Sarah Michelle Gellar's title character throughout its seven seasons. More recently, he appeared in the Emmy-winning comedy series Ted Lasso, where he played former football club owner Rupert Mannion and worked alongside co-creator Jason Sudeikis, receiving praise for their on-screen chemistry.

Beyond these major roles, Head's career was remarkably diverse. He appeared in the BBC production of Merlin and had a recurring role in the sketch comedy show Little Britain, where he played a British prime minister. He also appeared in films including The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie.

Before his television success, Head had an extensive stage career. He starred in the 1978 West End revival of Godspell and later performed in the original West End production of the Abba musical Chess in 1988. He also played Dr Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show.

In the 1980s, Head became well-known in the UK and US for his role in Nescafe Gold Blend television advertisements, which featured a slow-burn courtship between a British couple. During that same period, he sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box and was featured on their 1986 debut album.

Head was born in Camden, London, to artistic parents. His father was a documentary filmmaker who founded Verity Films, while his mother was an actor who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother was also an actor, known for his lead role in the 1971 film Sunday Bloody Sunday.

Following news of his death, cast members from Buffy the Vampire Slayer paid tribute to their former colleague. Sarah Michelle Gellar shared a tribute on Instagram, beginning with a quote from her Buffy character before reflecting on her loss. His daughters noted that their father loved his work and considered himself fortunate to have worked with talented people throughout his career spanning several decades.

"We know his legacy will live on in the shows he was a part of and in the audiences that love them," his daughters said.

cards.headline: Singer Duffy to perform first concert in over 15 years
cards.teaser: The Welsh singer announced her return to live performance after stepping away from public life following a sexual assault.
cards.body:
Welsh singer Duffy has announced her first live concert in more than 15 years, marking a significant return to performing. The artist, who achieved commercial success with her 2008 debut album Rockferry and hit songs like "Mercy," has been largely absent from public life since the early 2010s.

Duffy previously revealed that a sexual assault prompted her to step away from her music career and public appearances. The upcoming concert represents her return to the stage following this extended hiatus.

cards.headline: Shivani Pandya Malhotra leaves Red Sea Film Festival director role
cards.teaser: The managing director stepped down from the Saudi Arabian festival after helping establish it as a major regional cultural event.
cards.body:
Shivani Pandya Malhotra has stepped down as general manager of Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Film Festival. She had been instrumental in building the event from its inception and guiding it through five editions.

Under her leadership, the festival grew into one of the Arab world's most prominent film events and became the leading movie market in the Middle East and North Africa region.

cards.headline: Sean Penn skipped Oscars ceremony despite winning Best Supporting Actor
cards.teaser: The actor cited mental health reasons for missing the Academy Awards where he won for One Battle After Another.
cards.body:
Sean Penn was absent from this year's Academy Awards ceremony despite winning the Best Supporting Actor Oscar. Penn won the award for his performance in One Battle After Another but did not attend to accept the statuette in person.

The actor later stated that he skipped the ceremony for mental health reasons. Penn also mentioned in a recent interview that he dislikes taking selfies, offering insight into his general aversion to certain aspects of public attention and celebrity culture.

cards.headline: Zegna hosts fashion show at Malibu Pier with celebrity guests
cards.teaser: Italian fashion house Zegna staged a summer collection showcase with attendees including Rami Malek and Mahershala Ali.
cards.body:
Italian fashion house Zegna hosted a summer fashion show at Malibu Pier on Friday night. Male models dressed in white and carrying umbrellas greeted guests along the driveway, while the venue served colorful cocktails.

The event attracted a notable group of celebrity attendees, including actors Rami Malek, Mahershala Ali, Stellan Skarsgård, and Paul Dano, along with model Soo Joo Park. The scenic beachside location served as the backdrop for the brand's seasonal collection presentation.

cards.headline: Fans speculate about Taylor Swift wedding plans
cards.teaser: Followers of the singer are searching for clues about potential nuptials with NFL player Travis Kelce.
cards.body:
Swifties around the world are searching for clues about a potential wedding between Taylor Swift and NFL star Travis Kelce. The couple's high-profile relationship has sparked widespread fan speculation about possible nuptials.

Supporters have been analyzing social media posts and public appearances, trying to forecast details about any upcoming ceremony. The intense focus reflects the significant attention their relationship has generated across both the music and sports worlds.

cards.headline: Elmo faces criticism from Knicks fans over NBA Finals stance
cards.teaser: The Sesame Street character was called a traitor by New York basketball fans for not fully supporting the city's team.
cards.body:
Elmo, the Sesame Street character whose fictional home is in New York, faced backlash from Knicks fans after taking a stance on the NBA Finals that didn't fully support the city's basketball team. Fans called the character a traitor for not showing complete hometown allegiance during the championship series.

The incident underscores the passionate loyalty New York fans have for the Knicks, with expectations that even beloved fictional characters demonstrate unwavering support for the team.

hero.headline: Justice Department ends Trump administration anti-weaponization fund
hero.body:
The Justice Department told a federal court that the Trump administration's compensation fund for people who claimed they were targets of government weaponization will not continue. Two DOJ attorneys filed the notice in the Eastern District of Virginia, formally ending the nearly $1.8 billion program.

The fund was created by the Trump administration to compensate individuals who believed they were wrongly investigated or prosecuted for political reasons. The Justice Department's filing asked the court to reject a legal challenge brought by a former federal prosecutor and several other individuals related to the program.

The compensation fund represented one of the Trump administration's initiatives to address what it characterized as political targeting by federal law enforcement. The program's total budget allocation reached $1.8 billion before the Justice Department moved to discontinue it.

The court filing provides official confirmation that the program has been terminated. The former federal prosecutor and other plaintiffs had brought their challenge in Virginia's Eastern District, one of the busiest federal court districts in the country. The Justice Department's request for dismissal of that challenge coincided with its announcement that the fund would cease operations.

The end of the anti-weaponization fund marks a significant policy reversal. No information was provided about whether any compensation had been distributed before the program's termination or what will happen to the funds that had been set aside for the initiative.

cards.headline: Trump discusses price pressures on farmers at rally
cards.teaser: President Trump acknowledged farmers are facing higher costs for fertilizer and fuel during a rally appearance.
cards.body:
President Trump addressed agricultural price pressures during a rally, acknowledging that farmers are experiencing higher costs for fertilizer and fuel. Supporters at the event cheered for ending war, though the specific conflict was not detailed in his remarks.

Trump also spent significant time discussing Washington landmarks during his speech, including the city's fountains and the Reflecting Pool. The remarks came as the agricultural sector faces economic challenges from increased input costs.

cards.headline: USDA confirms second screwworm parasite case in Texas
cards.teaser: The Agriculture Department confirmed a second flesh-eating screwworm found in a Texas calf as officials work to contain the outbreak.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed a second case of New World screwworm in Texas after identifying the parasite in a one-month-old calf in Zavala County. The discovery prompted Texas to declare a state of disaster over the outbreak.

In response to the threat, Canada has implemented a ban on cattle imports from Texas. The USDA is working to contain and eradicate the outbreak before the flesh-eating parasite causes widespread damage to the livestock population.

cards.headline: Forest Service plans to close research facilities despite budget questions
cards.teaser: The Forest Service is moving to shut down research hubs to cut costs, but plans to close low-cost facilities while keeping expensive ones open.
cards.body:
The Forest Service announced plans to shut down research hubs as part of cost-cutting efforts. However, the agency's strategy has drawn scrutiny for its inconsistency.

The closures target facilities that cost less than $1 annually to rent, yet the Forest Service plans to keep at least one facility operating that costs $1 million per year. This disparity raises questions about whether the closures will meaningfully reduce expenses or achieve the agency's stated goal of operating within budget constraints.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, the former Interior Secretary under President Biden, won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. If elected in November, she would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States.

Haaland previously served in Congress representing New Mexico before becoming the first Native American cabinet secretary in the Biden administration.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra takes top spot in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra won the most votes in California's gubernatorial primary, securing a place in November's general election.
cards.body:
Xavier Becerra, former Health and Human Services Secretary under President Biden, has secured the top spot on California's November gubernatorial ballot. The Democrat emerged from a crowded primary field in the race to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom.

Election officials continue counting ballots to determine Becerra's general election opponent. His challenger will be either fellow Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist who has advocated for universal healthcare and higher taxes on billionaires, or Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality endorsed by Donald Trump.

cards.headline: Judge orders former CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars to remain jailed
cards.teaser: A federal judge denied release for a former CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars, but said the defense could request another hearing with new evidence.
cards.body:
A judge ruled that a former CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars must remain in jail pending trial. The defendant, identified as Rush, had sought release but the court denied the request.

The judge told defense attorneys they could request another hearing if they find new evidence supporting Rush's release. The case involves allegations that the former intelligence officer stole gold bars, though further details about the theft were not provided.
